title: Understanding Trap Seals and Venting
description: Proper drainage system design relies heavily on functional fixture traps and adequate venting to protect indoor air quality and maintain smooth water flow. A trap seal consists of a small amount of water retained within the U-bend of the fixture trap, which physically blocks sewer gases from entering the living space. Without a balanced venting system, the discharge of wastewater from upper fixtures can create negative or positive air pressures that siphon this crucial water barrier away. Professional drainage installation requires careful attention to vent placement and trap design to ensure continuous atmospheric pressure equalization, preventing both trap siphoning and slow-draining fixtures.

Understanding Trap Seals and Venting

Proper drainage system design relies heavily on functional fixture traps and adequate venting to protect indoor air quality and maintain smooth water flow. A trap seal consists of a small amount of water retained within the U-bend of the fixture trap, which physically blocks sewer gases from entering the living space. Without a balanced venting system, the discharge of wastewater from upper fixtures can create negative or positive air pressures that siphon this crucial water barrier away. Professional drainage installation requires careful attention to vent placement and trap design to ensure continuous atmospheric pressure equalization, preventing both trap siphoning and slow-draining fixtures.
